sections.name: register
sections.title: Startup for server and edge
sections.what: When the server starts, checks whether it is running on the Node or edge runtime and starts Sentry with the matching settings. Also exposes the hook that reports failed server requests.
sections.why: Each runtime needs its own Sentry start, so errors are captured wherever the code runs.
sections.watch_out: If the two branches get different settings later, errors may be recorded differently depending on where they happen.

summary: Starts Sentry error monitoring on the server side of the Next.js app, for the Node and edge runtimes.
purpose: Records errors that happen on the server, so developers can see problems that users never see in their browser.
why: Next.js runs server code in two different environments. This file starts Sentry in each one. The reason for the split is partly visible: each environment gets its own setup.
how: Next.js calls the register function when the server starts. The function checks which runtime is running and starts Sentry with the same address and a ten percent trace sample. It also exports the request error hook that Next.js calls when a server request fails.
inputs: The NEXT_RUNTIME value set by Next.js, and the NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN environment variable.
outputs: Server error reports and traces sent to Sentry.
risks: Both branches repeat the same settings, so a change to one branch can be missed in the other. Server errors can include sensitive request data unless Sentry is set to filter it.
debug: If server errors do not reach Sentry, confirm the register function runs at startup and that the DSN variable is set on the server. Check the runtime value in logs.
